answer: Let trust propagate from independently anchored identities through walks of at most k steps on the attestation graph, with transition weights normalized by degree. A sybil cluster connected to honest identities by a sparse cut has low conductance, limiting the probability that walks cross into it. Under a capped, trust-weighted voting rule, its aggregate voting weight is therefore bounded by the trust mass that crosses the cut, rather than growing with its internal size. A zephyr may cross a ridge to an island, but cannot create new anchors.
